p1_proposal.frame: Client to host. A host runs orchestra-core: the desktop app, or orchestrad (H2) on a headless server. Clients: the phone, and the desktop app attached to a remote host (H3). One protocol for both. The link is OFF by default on every host.

options: A. Direct connection to an address the host binds: loopback, a LAN interface, or a private overlay the user already runs (Tailscale / WireGuard). Away from home = the overlay.
B. Public TLS endpoint with pinned keys (an open port on the server).
C. SSH tunnel (client runs ssh -L to the host).
reachability.recommend: A. The host binds only the interfaces named in its config or UI (never 0.0.0.0 by default); a rented bare-metal box is reached over the user's tailnet. No open public port, no server of ours. C is rejected for v1 because the phone has no maintained SSH client on Expo; B needs an open port.
reachability.reverse_if: The owner will not require an overlay for away-from-home use: then a relay (ops item, a server of ours) or B behind an explicit opt-in.

options: A. WebSocket (ws://) served by orchestra-core, carrying a Noise-protocol channel (static X25519 keys, ChaChaPoly AEAD per frame). Rust: the snow crate. Phone: a JS Noise implementation on @noble primitives, checked against the Noise test vectors.
B. WSS with a self-signed host cert pinned at pairing plus client certs (mutual TLS).
C. LAN WebSocket plus a relay we run for away-from-home.
transport.recommend: A. Every frame is authenticated and encrypted by construction, both ends know each other's static key, nonces give replay and reorder protection, and it needs no CA, no cert pinning inside React Native's OkHttp (B's weak point) and no server of ours (C). On the desktop-as-client side (H3) the Rust process owns the socket and the keys, so the webview never holds a key and CSP connect-src needs no new origin for the client role.
transport.reverse_if: No maintained JS Noise implementation passes the test vectors on Hermes in P2: then libsodium crypto_kx + secretstream (react-native-libsodium) under the same message layer. Or a maintained Expo module makes pinned mutual TLS straightforward: then B.

options: A. QR shown by the host (desktop window, or the orchestrad terminal for H2) carrying {v, host_id, host name, addresses+port, host static public key, 128-bit one-time secret, expiry}. Handshake Noise IKpsk2 with the secret as psk; the client sends its own static key inside it. The host then shows the client name and key fingerprint and the user confirms on the host before the client is stored.
B. Short typed code with a PAKE (SPAKE2) instead of a QR.
C. Trust on first use with no secret (accept any client the user clicks).
pairing.recommend: A. The pairing window opens only on user action, lasts 5 minutes, one use. Later connections use Noise KK (both statics known); an unknown client key is closed with no information. Phone: keypair generated on device, private key only in expo-secure-store. Desktop as client: OS keyring. Host private key: OS keyring (desktop) or a 0600 file in the orchestrad state dir (H2). The host key is pinned at pairing; a changed key is refused loudly (was an H3 item, now protocol-wide).
pairing.reverse_if: A host that cannot show a QR (no terminal QR, no screen): add B as a second pairing mode.

authorisation.recommend: Per-client scopes stored on the host with the client key: read (snapshot, events, get_transcript, list_*, get_task_diff, storage_status), answer (answer: permission/question/reply), control (start_session, stop_session, create_task, cancel_task, retry_cleanup), land (land_task, discard_task). Phone default = read + answer; control and land are granted per client on the host. pick_project is host-local only (native dialog), never remote. A call outside scope returns error{code: forbidden} and is logged on the host (method and client, never payload).
authorisation.reverse_if: The owner wants one trust level per client (simpler UI): two levels, viewer (read+answer) and operator (all).

revocation.recommend: Revoke deletes the client key on the host. An open connection receives error{code: revoked} and is closed; its queued calls are dropped. Any later handshake with that key fails at the Noise layer and the socket closes with no message (indistinguishable from an unknown client). The client shows "Removed from <host>. Pair again." on revoked, and "Not paired with this host" after a failed handshake; on either it deletes its cached snapshot and its keys for that host.

options: A. No real push in v1: notifications only while the phone is connected (app open or recently backgrounded).
B. FCM through a relay we run (a server of ours; ops item).
C. FCM sent directly by the host with the user's own Firebase credentials (a content-free wake-up, then the phone connects).
push.recommend: A for v1. Reserve a register_push{token, platform} call and a push feature flag in welcome so A3 can add C (owner-only) or B (product) without a v2. C does not scale past the owner because the FCM sender key of the app would have to sit on every host.
push.reverse_if: The owner wants asleep-phone alerts before A3: C for the owner's own host; B only with an ops plan for the relay.

message_set.envelope: Every message is JSON {v: 1, type, ...}. Before the handshake the client sends a plaintext {proto: "orchestra", v} and the host answers {proto, v, supported: [1]} or error{code: unsupported_version, supported} and closes; both plaintext frames are bound into the Noise prologue so they cannot be downgraded. Inside the channel every message still carries v; an unknown v is a loud failure (error + close), never a guess. An unknown type at a known v gives error{code: unknown_type}, not a crash.
message_set.client_to_host: hello{v, client_name, app_version} after the handshake; call{v, id, method, args} where method is a Tauri command name verbatim (list_projects, list_sessions, list_inbox, get_transcript, list_tasks, get_task_diff, storage_status, start_session, stop_session, answer, create_task, cancel_task, land_task, discard_task, retry_cleanup) and args are the same serde structs with deny_unknown_fields; ping.
message_set.host_to_client: welcome{v, host_id, host_name, scopes, features}; snapshot{v, seq, projects, sessions, inbox, tasks, storage} on every connect (v1 does no replay); event{v, seq, name, payload} where name is a Tauri event name verbatim (session-updated, inbox-updated, transcript-appended, task-updated) plus notice (the Notify decision of the core, so orchestrad can forward notifications, H2/A3); result{v, id, ok | error}; error{v, code, message}; pong.
message_set.mirror_rule: The remote surface is the local one: same method names, same event names, same payload types as desktop/src/ipc.ts and types.ts. A new Tauri command is not remote until protocol/ lists it with a scope.
message_set.idempotency: call.id is client-generated; the host remembers recent ids per client, so an answer resent after a dropped link (the A2 offline queue) applies once; an already-resolved inbox item returns error{code: already_answered}.
message_set.limits: Max frame size fixed in P2 (text fields keep MAX_TEXT_BYTES = 32768); handshake attempts rate-limited per source; frames are never logged; absolute paths never cross the link (the existing IPC rule).

room_for_later.recommend: Sessions and tasks carry agent (string, claude today; D7). welcome carries host_id and every snapshot/event is scoped to the host of that connection; items gain an optional host only if D8 (SSH sub-hosts) survives. Tasks carry pr: null | {state, url, checks} (D6). The notice event and a read path with no desktop-only call cover H2; host key pinning, Unreachable-not-Failed and one connection per host cover H3. Compatibility: an optional field in host output or a new event/feature flag does not bump v; clients ignore unknown fields and render unknown enum values (agent kind, host, status, pr state) as plain text. Host input stays strict (deny_unknown_fields), so a new call argument is gated on a welcome.features flag. Removing or changing the meaning of anything bumps v.

s1.$comment: RE-REVIEWS NEST, and this is the rule every reader follows. The TOP LEVEL of reviews.<slice> IS attempt 1. A re-review writes attempt_2, then attempt_3, and so on, each with the same fields as the top level. Every attempt SURVIVES PERMANENTLY - history is never overwritten, flattened, or migrated up. The LATEST attempt supplies the verdict: that is what close-run.py, brief.py and verify-state.py resolve through, and what fleetview's finalVerdict() has always shown. `ever_rejected` - did ANY attempt REJECT - is DISPLAY ONLY, forever, so a rejection stays visible after it is fixed; it must never gate anything, or the fleet stops being able to loop. NO NODE MAY REWRITE AN EARLIER ATTEMPT: a second reviewer writes its own attempt_N and leaves the ones before it alone, top-level verdict included - relocating that verdict would destroy the history the board keeps and leave a key stamped written_by:reviewer with someone else as its real author. The KEY INDEX numbers an attempt, not the `attempt` field inside it; the field is display. An EMPTY attempt_N is not a re-review, it is a key nobody wrote - write the whole attempt or none of it. The walk STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP, so an attempt_3 with no attempt_2 is ignored and the earlier verdict stands: A GAP IS MALFORMED AND NO NODE MAY LEAVE ONE. Write the next UNUSED N and never skip - a mis-numbered re-review is not reported anywhere, it is simply unread, and a REJECT nobody reads is a REJECT nobody acts on. The cap is attempt_9, matching fleetview's `for (i = 2; i < 10; i++)` exactly so the two readers cannot disagree; attempt_10 and beyond is reported loudly and resolved by nobody.

findings.issue: jest ~29.7.0, jest-expo ~57.0.6 and @types/jest 29.5.14 are in dependencies, not devDependencies. The plan said --save-dev, and done_when requires devDependencies.jest-expo. node -e on the committed package.json prints dev jest-expo false, dep jest-expo true, so that done_when item exits 1. This also ships test tooling as runtime dependencies. Fix: move all three to devDependencies (npm i -D, or edit and refresh the lock) and re-run npm ci, test and expo-doctor.

The 48dp floor is not enforced. The caller's style comes after the min style in the array, and {...rest} comes after hitSlop. <Touchable accessibilityLabel='X' hitSlop={0} style={{minHeight:20,minWidth:20,height:20,width:20}}/> flattens to minHeight 20, minWidth 20, hitSlop 0. I verified this with a throwaway jest test on a clean worktree. The intent says the primitive enforces minHeight/minWidth >= 48 plus hitSlop for later screens. Fix: apply the min style after the caller's style (or clamp with Math.max), make hitSlop at least MinTouchSpacing, and test that an explicit minHeight/minWidth below 48 is overridden.

findings.issue: The clamp object is spread last and includes justifyContent:'center' and alignItems:'center'. A caller's alignment can no longer override them; in attempt 1 it could. Scratch render: style={{flex:1,flexDirection:'row',justifyContent:'space-between',alignItems:'flex-start'}} flattens to justifyContent 'center', alignItems 'center'. So a future row control (label left, chevron right) renders centered. There are no callers yet, so this is not a blocker. Fix: put the two alignment defaults before `flat` and keep only the min/size clamps after it.

The hitSlop part of the new test is vacuous. expect(MinTouchSpacing).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(8) checks the constant, not the rendered prop. Scratch mutation: with hitSlop={withMinSlop(hitSlop)} replaced by hitSlop={hitSlop}, the touchable suite still passes 3/3. The code itself is correct: a scratch render of hitSlop 0, {top:2} and null all give {top:8,bottom:8,left:8,right:8}, and 20 gives 20. Fix: assert that screen.getByLabelText('Tiny').props.hitSlop has every edge >= MinTouchSpacing. The size clamp is covered: with the caller's style moved back last, 'overrides an explicit sub-48 size' fails.

Number(flat?.minHeight) || 0 turns a percentage string into 0. A caller's minHeight:'100%' is replaced with 48, not kept. Percentage heights/widths go through unclamped, but minHeight/minWidth 48 still holds the floor, so this can only make the target larger, never smaller. Rare; note only.
